source.title: Wormhole Dynamics in Deep Neural Networks

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present; no apparent cutoff or garbling that prevents extraction.
record.tranche_reason: The study reports results on unseen samples using its own unsupervised analytical procedure, a setting distinct from the claim's supervised natural-label training recipes.
record.gate_note: The paper reports results for unsupervised feature collapse and label reconciliation. Its references to random-label memorization and other generalization findings are cited background, not results from this study. The measured clustering and classification outcomes do not test the specific behaviors named in V1–V8.
record.test_reason: The study measures feature collapse, clustering and flipped-image distribution separation under a custom analytical procedure. None measures the comparisons specified in V1–V8. Random-label fitting and standard generalization findings appear as background; constructed image reconciliation does not test V1.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially accurate. The authors attribute unseen-input clustering to feature collapse under analytical norm maximization and normalization, and propose a wormhole solution for constructed label reconciliation. They interpret these results as explaining generalization and shortcut learning, while leaving convolutional and transformer extensions to future work. These interpretations do not establish any V1–V8 comparison.
record.recipe_differences: Uses an analytical maximum-likelihood procedure with norm maximization and normalization in feedforward linear networks; it does not use the standard supervised gradient-based training recipes in the claim.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports clustering metrics improving with depth and width, and decidability increasing over L = 1, 2, 3, 4. Exact plotted values are not stated in the text.

fits_no_version.finding: Section V.B reports increasing Silhouette Score and inter-cluster distance, and decreasing Davies-Bouldin Index and intra-cluster distance with depth on unseen Gaussian inputs.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The proposed analytical linear-network procedure produces increasingly separated and compact output clusters with depth.

fits_no_version.finding: Section VI.A reports increasing d′ across depths 1–4 for unseen MNIST zero images and their sign-flipped counterparts.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Increasing depth improves output-distribution separation for original versus sign-flipped images under this single-example feature-learning procedure.

fits_no_version.finding: Section VIII.A reports visual recovery of MNIST images from constructed perturbations with scale 10000 as depth increases.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The proposed procedure can reconcile images with perturbations constructed from its own normalized output vectors.

record.peer_reviewed: IEEE Transactions on Neural Networks and Learning Systems
record.problems: The reported experiments use the paper's custom unsupervised procedure rather than standard supervised gradient training. Several numerical outcomes are presented in figures without textual values. The paper itself says extension to convolutional and transformer architectures remains future work.
record.rows_left_out: No eligible results were omitted. Cited background findings were excluded because they are not results of this study.

untested.parts: Coexistence of random-label fitting and natural-label generalization under the same architecture and recipe, including chance held-out accuracy for random labels.
Test error as width increases beyond the width required for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image-classification performance and the contribution of local connectivity or initialization.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under limited or broader tuning, weight-decay changes or optimizer switching.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that reduce those effects.
Dropout effects on held-out error across data sizes, dropout strengths and augmentation regimes.
Magnitude-aware sharpness versus generalization gaps and alternative measures.
Test-accuracy effects of removing highly memorized versus randomly selected training examples.

record.verdict_notes: Change the record's tests/T3 classification to discusses/T6. Row states are cannot_determine relative to V1–V8; the reported clustering and d′ trends themselves are present. Algorithm 1's row-selection step, called dropout by the authors, supplies no dropout-versus-control test of V6.

versions.untested_parts: Does not fit fixed random labels and compare held-out random-label and natural-label accuracy under the same standard training recipe.
Does not sweep width past the zero-training-error threshold on MNIST or downsampled CIFAR-10 and measure test error.
Does not compare convolutional and fully connected image classifiers.
Does not compare adaptive optimizers with SGD or momentum SGD.
Does not compare batch sizes under fixed epoch budgets.
Does not test dropout or its removal with weight decay.
Does not measure magnitude-aware sharpness or compare it with generalization gaps.
Does not remove memorized training examples and measure the resulting test accuracy.

tranche.reason: The analytical feature-collapse, clustering and distribution-separation results measure none of V1–V8's comparisons. Constructed label reconciliation does not test random-label fitting and natural-label held-out accuracy under the same recipe.
